user.title: Climate Orchestrator
user.description: Select the radiator valves (TRVs) and air conditioners to orchestrate. Sensors are matched automatically from each device's Home Assistant area.

data.home_temperature_sensor: Whole-home average temperature sensor (optional, overrides the computed average)

data_description.trvs: The radiator-valve climate entities to orchestrate.
data_description.acs: The air-conditioner climate entities to orchestrate.
data_description.outdoor_sensor: Used for outdoor gating and adaptive cooling comfort.
data_description.weather_entity: Provides the hourly forecast for preconditioning.
data_description.home_temperature_sensor: Replaces the computed whole-home average temperature; falls back to computed if unavailable.
data_description.home_humidity_sensor: Replaces the computed whole-home average humidity; falls back to computed if unavailable.
data_description.ac_drain_sensor: A binary sensor that turns on when an AC's condensate tank needs emptying. While on past the grace window, the AC is held off until it clears.
data_description.presets: Which presets to offer on the thermostat. Only selected presets get editable setpoint entities; manual setpoints are always available.
data_description.valve_opening_hints: Name fragments used to discover each TRV's valve-opening number entity (MPC mode).
data_description.calibration_hints: Name fragments used to discover each TRV's local-calibration number entity (offset mode).

error.no_devices: Select at least one radiator valve or air conditioner.

no_maintenance_valves.message: No valve-opening number entities were found for the selected TRVs. Check the valve name hints in the integration's options.

missing_calibration_number.title: Climate Orchestrator: TRV calibration number not found
missing_calibration_number.description: The radiator valve `{entity_id}` is set to `{mode}` calibration mode, but Climate Orchestrator couldn't find its `valve_opening_degree` / `local_temperature_calibration` number entity. That mode can't act, so the valve falls back to plain target control. Either switch the TRV calibration mode back to `target`, or check that the valve exposes the expected number (Zigbee2MQTT naming).

outdoor_sensor_missing.title: Climate Orchestrator: outdoor sensor needed
outdoor_sensor_missing.description: Adaptive comfort and/or outdoor temperature gating are enabled, but no outdoor temperature sensor is configured, so those features do nothing. Add an outdoor sensor (or weather entity) in the integration's Configure dialog, or turn the features off.

no_temperature_source.title: Climate Orchestrator: no temperature source
no_temperature_source.description: Climate Orchestrator has no usable temperature reading for any managed device, so it can't decide whether to heat or cool. Assign a temperature sensor to each device's area under Settings → Areas → Related sensors.

stale_sensor.title: Climate Orchestrator: stale sensor reading
stale_sensor.description: One or more area sensors have stopped updating for longer than the configured staleness timeout, so Climate Orchestrator is ignoring their values and falling back to the home average. Check the affected sensor's battery/connection, or raise the **Sensor staleness timeout** number if your sensors legitimately report slowly.

ac_drain_sensor_unavailable.title: Climate Orchestrator: AC drain sensor unavailable
ac_drain_sensor_unavailable.description: AC drain protection is on and a condensate drain / tank-full sensor is configured, but that sensor is missing or unavailable. Protection fails open while it can't be read (cooling is never cut by a sensor it can't trust), so your overflow protection is currently inactive. Check the sensor's battery/connection, or turn **AC drain protection** off if you removed it. This notice clears once the sensor reports again.

control_loop_failing.title: Climate Orchestrator: control cycle repeatedly failing
control_loop_failing.description: The control cycle has failed several times in a row, so your devices are no longer receiving fresh commands (sensor readings still update). Check the Home Assistant log for the underlying error — it usually points at an unresponsive device or integration. This notice clears itself on the next successful cycle.

device_ignoring_commands.title: Climate Orchestrator: device ignoring commands
device_ignoring_commands.description: Commands to `{entity_id}` are being accepted, but the device's state has not reflected the requested HVAC mode for several minutes — it is silently ignoring them. Common causes: a child/temperature lock engaged on the device, a weak Zigbee/radio link, a dying battery, or its integration no longer talking to the hardware. Until it complies, this room is not actually being controlled. This notice clears itself as soon as the device applies a command.

inverted_band.title: Climate Orchestrator: comfort band inverted
inverted_band.description: The active comfort band has its cool setpoint *below* its heat setpoint, leaving no neutral zone — the system will heat below the cool edge and cool above it, running almost constantly. Check the active preset's heat/cool setpoints (the heat setpoint should be the lower of the two).

weather_forecast_missing.title: Climate Orchestrator: weather entity needed
weather_forecast_missing.description: Forecast preconditioning is enabled, but no weather entity is configured, so there's no forecast to plan against and the feature does nothing. Add a weather entity in the integration's Configure dialog, or turn Forecast preconditioning off.

weather_forecast_unavailable.title: Climate Orchestrator: weather forecast unavailable
weather_forecast_unavailable.description: Forecast preconditioning is enabled and a weather entity is configured, but its hourly forecast has been unavailable for hours — the `weather.get_forecasts` call keeps failing or returns no usable data. Preconditioning is silently inert as a result (control still works; it just can't pre-heat ahead of a cold spell). Check that the weather entity supports an hourly forecast and is working, or turn Forecast preconditioning off. This notice clears once a forecast is fetched again.

heating_assist_unavailable.title: Climate Orchestrator: heating assist can't heat
heating_assist_unavailable.description: **AC heating assist** is enabled, but no available air conditioner can heat — either none is selected, or the selected one(s) don't offer a `heat` HVAC mode. The orchestrator decides the AC should help heat, then has no way to command it, so nothing happens. Select an air conditioner that supports heating (a reverse-cycle / heat-pump unit) in the integration's Configure dialog, or turn AC heating assist off.

dehumidify_unavailable.title: Climate Orchestrator: dehumidify guard can't dry
dehumidify_unavailable.description: **Dew point guard** is enabled and an air conditioner is configured, but none of the available units offer a `dry` HVAC mode, so muggy air can't trigger dehumidification. Use an air conditioner that supports a dry mode, or turn Dew point guard off.

ac_ignore_window_inert.title: Climate Orchestrator: window exemption has no AC
ac_ignore_window_inert.description: **AC ignores open windows** is enabled, but no air conditioner is configured, so the exemption has nothing to apply to. Select an air conditioner in the integration's Configure dialog, or turn the setting off.

mpc_model_poor_fit.title: Climate Orchestrator: MPC model can't fit this radiator
mpc_model_poor_fit.description: The MPC thermal model for `{entity_id}` has fit its room poorly for over a day — its learned `gain`/`loss` no longer explain how the room actually responds. The usual cause is a **weather-compensated** heating system (district heating, or a boiler on an outdoor-reset curve): the supply-water temperature rises in cold weather, so the same valve opening emits more heat than the model's single constant `gain` can represent. Control still keeps the room comfortable via feedback, but preconditioning is less reliable and you may see mild over/undershoot when the weather shifts. On such systems, switching this TRV's calibration mode to **offset** (which lets the valve's own loop modulate against the live water temperature) is usually the better choice. This notice clears itself once the model fits again.

reset_mpc_learning.name: Reset MPC learning
reset_mpc_learning.description: Forget the learned MPC thermal model (heating power / heat loss) for some or all radiator valves, so they re-learn from scratch.

trvs.name: Radiator valves
trvs.description: Which TRV climate entities to reset. Leave empty to reset all.

run_valve_maintenance.name: Run valve maintenance
run_valve_maintenance.description: Exercise the radiator valves by driving them fully open and then closed, which prevents them seizing or scaling when held at one position for a long time.

trvs.name: Radiator valves
trvs.description: Which TRV climate entities to exercise. Leave empty for all.
